floors.disqualifying_numbers: Narrowing the rails is replay-NEUTRAL-to-slightly-positive (no regression): F1 (graph_min->0) leaves live_weights unchanged and lifts replayed_proportional MRR 0.705265->0.705874; F2 (wide rails bm25_max0.95/vector_min0.05/graph_min0/bm25_min0.05) lifts replayed_proportional hit@5 0.948601->0.949902 and MRR 0.705265->0.705821. So narrowing does NOT improve the holdout metric materially AND the mean-share fixed point already does the real work within the current rails. The exact floor VALUES are pinned by ~9 existing test files (below); changing the defaults would rewrite those assertions, which gate (3) forbids.
floors.note: Floors protect exact-identifier and semantic recall and the graph-floor (properties verified by the pinning tests) that the grounded-holdout metric does not fully exercise; they are retained as narrow guardrails, not compensation for a starved signal.
floors.operator_path: maintenance.reseat_retrieval_floors (audited; dry-run is the default; apply writes only rows whose before!=after via per-scope set_retrieval_weights). Operators may narrow rails through this audited path; this tree performs NO automatic weight rewrites.

rescue.disqualifying_numbers: Removing the rescue (E2) OR restricting it to causal-only (E1) gives IDENTICAL holdout numbers (the causal 0.75 arm changes no holdout useful-result ranking; the value is entirely in the non-causal 0.25 arm) and REGRESSES vs R0: live_weights hit@5 0.947951->0.946649, MRR 0.703243->0.700532; replayed_proportional hit@5 0.948601->0.946649, MRR 0.705265->0.701717. The rescue still adds positive holdout value under honest credit + typed edges, so it is retained on evidence, not merely on test-compatibility.
rescue.location: src/living_memory/retrieval.py:224-232 (in-rank graph rescue, minimum_graph 0.25 non-causal / 0.75 causal)
rescue.note: Full removal / causal-only both also break the above existing tests, which gate (3) forbids weakening. Double-disqualified: replay regression + existing-test breakage.
